objective: Applying PRiSM life cycle phases to a scenario: staffing, deliverables, risk/opportunity management, cost/finance, and scheduling
secondaryObjectives: Identifying core PRiSM concepts and principles: how PRiSM relates to traditional project management, and the PRiSM Project Life Cycle's features and key deliverables

sources.cite: PMI, Certified Sustainable Project Professional (CSPP) bundle and exam page: P5 Standard: Sustainability and Impact Analysis 24% (the largest domain with PRiSM Life Cycle Approach 23% and Project Management Considerations 23%)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 directly (summarizing fetch of pmi.org/certifications/cspp-bundle-exam-course). The page lists six domains: Foundations of Sustainable Project Work 12%, PRiSM Life Cycle Approach 23%, P5 Standard: Sustainability and Impact Analysis 24%, Developing a Sustainability Management Plan 12%, ESG & Sustainability Reporting, Governance, and Project Communications 7%, Project Management Considerations 23% (they add to 101%). It says the P5 Standard evaluates project impacts on 'people, planet, and prosperity', and a prep module practices 'a P5 Impact Analysis' to 'identify, assess and mitigate sustainability impacts'. The course seed's five domains and weights (P5 36%) differ from this page; the P5 domain is the largest either way. The objective wording is the course seed's. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's cspp-school-laptop-p5-review (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The organization, the project, the figures and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You manage a fictional cooperative's community solar farm. The plan stops at commissioning; the panels will run 30 years and then need decommissioning.
handover: The cooperative's members want local benefit.
howItWorks: The board shows the risk register against the appetite, each stakeholder's support in words and the docket.
Move on a week at a time. A decision comes to you at each review; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Week 2: the bank's due diligence asks for a decommissioning provision; financing is delayed.
Week 3: members vote against the herbicide plan at the AGM and the maintenance contract must be re-tendered.
Week 4: the supplier's panels are detained at the border under forced-labor import rules; the build stops for months.

choices.label: Extend the deliverables to operation, maintenance and decommissioning, with a recycling plan and a decommissioning fund in the finance model

effects.log: The plan covers the whole life.

choices.feedback: A life-cycle approach plans beyond handover to operation and end of life.

choices.label: Add operation but not end of life
Keep the plan to commissioning
choices.feedback: Who removes and recycles the panels in 30 years is unknown.

choices.label: Add opportunities: sheep grazing under panels for vegetation management and a pollinator meadow, with owners and value
choices.feedback: Risk management covers opportunities to create value, not just threats.

choices.label: Plan herbicide for vegetation as cheapest
choices.feedback: It harms soil and members object; an opportunity is lost.

procPrompt.title: Which panel supplier?
procPrompt.context: The cheapest supplier can't show where its polysilicon comes from.

choices.label: Score bids on cost, supply-chain traceability, take-back for recycling and local maintenance, and pick the best value

effects.log: A traceable supplier with take-back wins.

choices.feedback: Sustainable procurement weighs supply chain and end of life with cost.

choices.label: Pick the cheapest and ask for an audit later
choices.feedback: The audit comes after the commitment.

choices.label: Pick the cheapest
choices.feedback: Untraceable supply chains can include forced labor.

scoring.modelReasoning: A sustainable life-cycle approach extends project thinking beyond handover to operation and end of life, manages opportunities as well as threats, and uses sustainable procurement (traceability, take-back) alongside cost.
